news_summary: Tempus AI reported Q2 2026 results on July 30, 2026: revenue $382.5M (+22% YoY), gross profit $246.5M (+26%), and its first quarterly GAAP profit -- net income of $5.6M (which included $98.5M of unrealized gains on marketable securities and $55.6M of stock-comp/payroll-tax expense) versus a $42.8M net loss a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA was $8.0M versus -$5.6M in Q2 2025. Oncology diagnostics volume grew 31% and data-licensing revenue grew 36%, with Data and Applications revenue up 28% YoY. Tempus raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.595-1.605B (~25% growth), guided Q3 2026 revenue to $405-410M, and reaffirmed roughly $65M of adjusted EBITDA for the year (guidance excludes any Personalis impact). The company also completed a $460M zero-coupon convertible notes offering, secured FDA approval for its tumor-only xT CDx companion-diagnostic assay, and delivered its first oncology foundation model to AstraZeneca. Strategically, Tempus announced a definitive agreement on July 20, 2026 to acquire genomics/MRD company Personalis for about $1.5B (Personalis holders get $16.25/share, ~28% premium to unaffected 30-day VWAP, structured as up to 100% stock with an option for Tempus to pay up to 50% in cash), opening access to the roughly $20B minimal-residual-disease oncology monitoring market; closing is expected late 2026 or early 2027 subject to Personalis shareholder and regulatory approval. The market's initial reaction to the deal was negative -- both TEM and PSNL shares fell (TEM down roughly 4-6.9%) on dilution, valuation-multiple, and execution concerns, and a shareholder-rights firm is reviewing whether Tempus's pre-existing ~12.5% stake in and partnership with Personalis created a conflict of interest that disadvantaged PSNL holders in the deal terms. Elsewhere, Tempus's oncology AI/data business kept generating news: it announced a strategic lab partnership with CellCarta around Aug 6, 2026, and shares surged over 10% on Aug 7, 2026 amid a broader AI-healthcare sector rally sparked by strong Doximity earnings. Despite the operational momentum, Piper Sandler and H.C. Wainwright both cut price targets in early August (to $56, from $58 and $64 respectively), and TEM shares have fallen sharply from a 52-week high of $104.32 to roughly $52-54 by mid-August 2026.

move_thesis: Bull case: Q2 2026 showed accelerating core-business momentum (22% revenue growth, 31% oncology-diagnostics volume growth, 36% data-licensing growth) and Tempus's first quarterly GAAP profit, plus continued platform validation (FDA approval for the xT CDx companion diagnostic, an AstraZeneca foundation-model delivery, and peer-reviewed Nature Medicine results for PRISM2) and a roughly $20B new addressable market opened by the pending Personalis MRD acquisition. A sector-wide AI-healthcare rally (Doximity earnings, the new CellCarta lab partnership) drove an 11%+ single-day pop on Aug 7. Bear case: the market's initial read on the $1.5B Personalis deal was negative -- both TEM and PSNL fell on dilution, a rich valuation multiple (~15.5x estimated 2027 EV/sales per one analyst), and execution concerns, plus a shareholder-rights review into whether Tempus's pre-existing PSNL stake created a conflict of interest in setting deal terms. Multiple analysts (Piper Sandler, H.C. Wainwright) cut price targets even after the earnings beat, and the stock has fallen from a 52-week high of $104.32 to roughly $52-54 by mid-August 2026 -- a decline that has outpaced the operational improvement, suggesting the market is discounting dilution/execution risk on the acquisition and the fact that profitability remains thin on an adjusted-EBITDA basis (~$8M against $382.5M of revenue).
